utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good afternoon on my behalf as well. We -- in order to hear the remainder of the evidence for today, we move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Shin, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. Just one housekeeping matter. In our 92 ter application we had noted one proposed addition -- associated exhibit, but upon further reflection, we will not be tendering that as an associated exhibit, so as a result, there will be no associated exhibits for the 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that information. No further witnesses. I would like to use a little bit of time to deal with two matters, the first very short. The Chamber wishes to inform the parties that on the 30th of May, 2013, we'll start our morning session at 9.00 a.m. as opposed to the usual 9.30 a.m. Then I would also like to deliver a decision which is a decision on the addition of three exhibits to the Prosecution's 65 ter exhibit list. On the 12th of April of this year, the Prosecution filed its seventh motion to add exhibits to its 65 ter exhibit list to tender through Witness Tomasz Blaszczyk, who is RM214, and Witness RM269. The Prosecution contends that the three proposed exhibits are relevant and of probative value, in particular with regard to the accused's whereabouts during the commission of crimes alleged in the indictment. The Prosecution seeks to amend its Rule 65 ter exhibit list at this stage as it only obtained information from Witness RM269 making the proposed exhibits relevant and only received it on the 26th of February, 2013. The Prosecution submits that the Defence will not suffer prejudice from this addition as they will have enough time to review them before the testimony of the witnesses. On the 26th of April, the Defence filed a response objecting to the motion in its entirety on the ground of lack of good cause, submitting that the Prosecution filed its motion to add these three exhibits to the Rule 65 ter list almost two months after it became aware of their relevance. The Chamber notes that the Defence has not disputed the relevance and probative value of the proposed exhibits, which consist of a one-page document, two aerial photographs, and a copy of an identification card. While the Chamber considers that the Prosecution could and should have sought the addition of these exhibits at an earlier stage and good cause for the delay has not been shown, it recalls that good cause is only one factor in the Chamber's consideration of whether the addition of proposed exhibits is in the interests of justice. The proposed exhibits are of prima facie relevance and of probative value and relate directly to the testimony of the two witnesses with whom they are to be used. Witness Blaszczyk and Witness RM269 are currently scheduled to testify in the week of the 20th of May and towards the middle of June 2013 respectively. Taking into account the limited length of the proposed exhibits, the Chamber finds that the accused will not be unduly prejudiced by their addition to the Prosecution's 65 ter exhibit list at this stage. Moreover, the Defence will be able to further address any prejudice it may have suffered from the late addition to the Rule 65 ter exhibit list when the documents are used and tendered by the Prosecution. In conclusion, the Chamber finds it to be in the interests of justice to grant the addition of the exhibits bearing provisional Rule 65 ter numbers 28786, 28787, and 28788. This concludes the Chamber's decision. If there are no further procedural matters to be raised -- I see, Mr. Groome, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know that Mr. McCloskey has informed the Chamber that there -- we'll not have sufficient evidence to fill all of the hearing time this week. I did want to remind the Chamber of a proposal I made last week to discuss how best to deal with evidence of a number of experts. I would suggest or request that we introduce that topic at some point this week and perhaps even if it's productive to speak about specific experts, I think that might allow greater efficiency later in the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber has already discussed your suggestion. I think the Chamber asked Mr. Lukic whether he had any position on the matter. If he has, we would even have time now to hear from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was a bit confused yesterday. I think it was raised yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I mixed the issues and I didn't address actually the right issue and we did not file anything since we received the e-mail from the OTP two, three days ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think the proposal and suggestion was to have an administrative hearing --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in which matters would be sorted out in relation to -- if I'm -- well, six expert witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And I guess what I'm suggesting now is that given there might be some time -- extra time this week, to deal with it this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid that we will not be ready this week. I just discussed it with my colleagues, and I don't think that we can be prepared to elaborate on this issue on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you prefer to deal with the matter in writing or would you rather --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's what we thought to ask Your Honours, to deal with the matter in writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Groome, any -- and is that after you will have met with the Prosecution - there's a lot of time for cups of tea and coffee over the days to come - or will it be that you respond without having met with the Prosecution to further discuss the matter? The Chamber would prefer a response after you had met.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably that would happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I was just thinking about it, Your Honour. To proceed in writing would be for the Prosecution to file a 92 bis application for each of these experts, and then in the response, I guess the Defence would indicate whether they had additional questions, and it would seem to me that just a short discussion just on the principle of whether this would be an appropriate way to proceed might be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to keep matters clear. Your suggestion was let's have a hearing or an administrative hearing on the matter. That was your proposal and suggestion. I expect Mr. Lukic to respond to that suggestion or proposal. It was not a formal motion, but I suggested that he would first meet with you to see whether you could resolve the matters among yourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe Mr. Groome does not want to meet with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm happy to meet with anyone who wants to discuss a way to make the trial more efficient. Mr. Lukic did suggest that we proceed in writing and I guess that's what I was responding to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then I suggested that it might be better that he first meet with you and then decide whether it's still -- whether he wants to respond in writing to your suggestion. We would not give him much time for that. I would say after discussion, he would be able to put that on paper within half a day or a day reasons why there still is any disagreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or perhaps at that point in time after the discussion with you, Mr. Groome, he may even prefer to then address the Chamber orally, and then we'll see where we are and whether there's any need to file any 92 bis or 92 ter motions in relation to those experts, and the Chamber will then consider how we will proceed, whether there's still a role to be played at that stage for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The Prosecution will proceed accordingly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Us too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then tomorrow we'll have two witnesses, and I do understand that the parties take an effort to see whether the evidence of the two witnesses could be concluded tomorrow. Is there any chance -- you'll save Friday coming to court if you would conclude tomorrow, if that is attractive for you. I see some smiles on the faces, which is a sufficient response to what I just said. We will adjourn for the day, and we will resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 16th of May, at 9.30 in the morning in this same Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 16th day of May, 2013, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.47 p.m.,
